cells.tense: One built thing in your life stands finished, and you are holding it steadily now.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Take the next stretch of a build you're in and carry your end without running it past anyone first. Your own reserves, your own pace, no reports. Let the result answer for itself.
cells.core:
What you've built holds. A project reached its shape, a room got finished, a document got signed, and you're near it still — not propping it up, just steady, able to let it be what it is. Days like this, hard weeks stay workable. You keep your grip and the ones nearby get the calm instead of the clench. Your end of the load gets carried, all of it, and it doesn't spill onto them.

Give the work in progress the same steadiness you give the finished thing. Take the part you'd usually run past someone first, or rush to be done with, and carry it on your own reserves for one stretch. When you want a check-in, let the work be the check. Steady hands don't need an audience to know the shape is right. They hold it and keep going, and the shape shows up by itself.
cells.sheetLine: You can be near what's built without holding it up.
cells.place: where what's done is let go

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future outcome that hasn't finished being built yet.
cells.ask: Before you check how something is landing, sit for five minutes with your hands quiet and nothing decided. Then look, and feel the first honest thing before you fix anything.
cells.core:
You're carrying the finished thing before it exists. Something is still in the middle — a build, a push, a year of work — and you've already moved ahead to the verdict. What will it mean, will it land, what to do when it doesn't. Your body is braced for news that isn't due. The work stopped being something you're doing and turned into something you're defending before the fight.

Steadiness, at this pitch, stops being steady. The front edge runs ahead of what exists. What's needed is the opposite muscle: open first. Before results arrive, before the next call has to be made, take an ordinary moment and leave it unchosen. Empty hands, nothing settled. The work doesn't need you braced. It needs you here when the real shape shows up.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a wall that hasn't been built yet.
cells.place: where what's done is let go

cells.tense: You are standing at an old finish line, looking ahead, while the start was already crossed.
cells.act: see the thing as if for the first time
cells.ask: Take the work you keep meaning to restart. Look at it as if you'd never seen it. Write what's actually there in a few plain lines — no history, no shoulds, no verdict. Read it back and let the plain facts decide.
cells.core:
An earlier build of yours reached its finish, or stopped where it stopped, and the part that would start the next thing is still facing that old threshold — waiting for it to open so the work can begin. From outside it can look like rest. From where you sit it's a held breath.

The next form doesn't come from pushing harder on the old one. It comes from seeing clearly. Take the work you keep meaning to pick back up and look at it as if for the first time. Put what's actually there into a few plain lines. No backstory, no verdict, no picture of how it should look. Just the ground as it sits today. Those lines are where you are, and the next move comes out of them.
cells.sheetLine: You're waiting at a threshold that's already been crossed.
cells.place: where what's done is let go

cells.tense: An ending is being signed in a room where your hand is already on the pen and no one has said your name.
cells.act: notice what is before your eyes before naming it
cells.ask: When something near you closes, catch yourself turning toward the ending before you've named it. Catch the moment you decide. Say nothing, do nothing. Once, then leave it.
cells.core:
You keep things in proportion. When a shared arrangement runs its course, or a way of working between people goes hollow, you're usually the one who quietly stops renewing it — no announcement, no scene, the thing ends and the table is clear before anyone notices the meal is over. From inside, this doesn't register as your doing. It registers as the thing simply ending.

The endings in your orbit have your hand in them. The clearing happens because you clear. That isn't a flaw to correct; it's a strength that runs without the lights on. Look at it before you interpret it. When something near you closes, catch the moment you turn toward the ending, before you've named what kind it is. One moment, noticed, then left be. Clear sight is enough; the ending is yours either way.
cells.sheetLine: You're signing the ending while saying the pen isn't yours.
cells.place: where what's done is let go
